title: Properties table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Properties of materials and habitats (Alchemy Island and Living Things and Their Habitats)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 9 (Properties table (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 9: Properties of materials. To understand that materials are chosen for their properties

questions.q: Why are saucepans made of metal?
questions.a: Metal is strong and does not melt on the cooker; it lets heat through to the food.
questions.model: What is the job? Cooking on heat. What property is needed? It must not melt and must let heat through. Metal does both. So saucepans are made of metal.

questions.a: For example: rubber, fabric, plastic film.

questions.q: Core: Choose 6 objects at home. Make a table: object, material, two properties.
questions.a: For example: spoon, steel, hard and strong; sock, cotton, soft and flexible.
questions.model: Teacher does the first: mug, ceramic, hard and waterproof.

questions.q: Extend: For two objects, explain why the material suits the job.
questions.a: For example: a sock is made of cotton because it is soft and flexible, so it is comfortable.

questions.q: Stretch: Suggest a better material for one object and say why.
questions.a: Accept a reasoned answer, e.g. a plastic cup for toddlers: it will not shatter if dropped.

questions.q: A material that bends without breaking is...
Big question: why is a window made of glass and not wood?
questions.a: Glass is transparent, so light comes in and we can see out; wood is opaque.
